title: Collective depinning of dipolar skyrmion chains: thermal and athermal rounding of an elastic polymer in a quenched landscape
authors: R. L. Silva, R. C. Silva, R. L. Stamps
abstract: The dynamics of interacting dipole skyrmion chains in a weak pinning landscape is studied through numerical solutions of the stochastic Thiele equation. Chains of different lengths with periodic boundary conditions are driven across quenched attractive pinning sites under different magnetic fields. A clear threshold spin current is identified as the critical depinning force. Three main results emerge: (i) for chains of 50 skyrmions or more, the depinning threshold is independent of chain length and remains close to one third of that of an isolated skyrmion. (ii) The transition rounding is only partly thermal: the width changes from w = 0.334 +/- 0.004 decades at T = 0 to 0.633 +/- 0.002 at 300 K, while the intrinsic Larkin correlation length remains about 2.6 bonds below kBT ~ V0/25. (iii) The width is nearly unchanged up to kBT ~ 0.14 V0, but increases almost fourfold by kBT ~ 0.23 V0, mainly through broadening of the creep regime. It is independent of chain length, ruling out finite-size rounding. Increasing the field from 30 to 40 mT changes the transition shape, widening its core by 26% while shortening the creep tails. For chains of about 200 skyrmions, depinning proceeds through a sequence of internal deformations - growth of the Larkin length and roughness, transient bond stretching, and subsequent recovery of mobility and Hall angle. These collective effects are relevant for skyrmion-based devices in which chains, rather than isolated textures, act as information carriers.
summary: This work analyzes how chains of magnetic skyrmions collectively depin from a random pinning landscape. Using simulations based on the stochastic Thiele equation, the authors show that the collective nature of the chain significantly lowers the critical depinning force compared to isolated skyrmions. This collective effect is robust and involves complex internal deformations during the transition.
main_problem: The study investigates the collective depinning dynamics of interacting dipolar skyrmion chains driven through a weak, quenched random pinning landscape.
main_result: The depinning threshold is found to be significantly lower (by a factor of three) for the collective chain compared to an isolated skyrmion, and this collective effect is robustly independent of the chain length.
method: The dynamics are simulated by numerically solving the stochastic Thiele equation, comparing results at zero temperature versus finite temperature.
model_or_system: The system models dipolar skyrmion chains as an elastic polymer interacting with a quenched random pinning potential. The dynamics are governed by the stochastic Thiele equation, incorporating pair interactions and pinning forces.
key_observables: Depinning threshold (critical force), transition rounding width, effective mobility, and Hall angle.
important_parameters: Temperature (T=0 vs 300 K), chain length (N=50 to 200), and applied magnetic field (30 to 40 mT).
main_assumptions: Non-bonded skyrmion forces are ignored, and the pinning potential is assumed to be weak enough to keep the skyrmion structure rigid.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate snapshots of the system, transport parameters (velocity, mobility, Hall angle) versus driving force, and the evolution of internal deformations during depinning.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical model using the stochastic Thiele equation, analyzes the depinning threshold and transition rounding at different temperatures, and concludes by detailing the sequence of internal deformations observed in longer chains.
why_interesting: The study of depinning in disordered media, particularly the comparison between collective vs. single-particle behavior, touches upon concepts of glassy dynamics and critical phenomena relevant to many-body physics in disordered potentials.
